title: Tensor and algebra adjunction for nonsymmetric operads
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Use ordinary small nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. For a small quasicategory $C$ and an operad $\mathcal O$, their categorical-pattern tensor $C\odot\mathcal O$ exists. It is the operadic fibrant replacement of the marked product $C\times\mathcal O\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with edges marked when their $C$-component is an equivalence and their $\mathcal O$-component is inert. For an operad $\mathcal Q$, let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal Q)$ be the full infinity category of functors $\mathcal O\to\mathcal Q$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving inert edges. There are coherent natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty}(C\odot\mathcal O,\mathcal Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(C,\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal Q)).$$
The tensor preserves small colimits separately in $C$ and $\mathcal O$. The assertions hold under universe enlargement: inclusion of the operads small in one universe into operads small in a containing universe preserves colimits indexed by simplicial sets small in the first universe. The displayed equivalence and separate preservation of such colimits also hold with $C$ and $\mathcal Q$ in the containing universe, with $C\odot\mathcal O$ and the mapping spaces then formed there. Fibrant replacement means a weak-equivalence map to a fibrant object in the nonsymmetric-operad model structure, whose cofibrations are monomorphisms and fibrant marked objects are precisely operads with inert edges marked; different replacements give equivalent operads.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] to the categorical pattern of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy] with $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, $S$ the inert arrows and, for each $n\geq0$, the cone from $[n]$ to its $n$ inert projections $[1]$. The leaves form the discrete $n$-element simplicial set, empty at $n=0$. The fiber-limit condition is $\mathcal O_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal O_{[1]}^n$. In the relative mapping-space pullback, the base mapping spaces are discrete sets of base arrows; its fiber over $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ is exactly the product formula in [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. Thus these are the ordinary operadic fibrant objects, including the terminal $[0]$-fiber and empty mapping product. [lem-coef-marked-operadic-model-structures] identifies this model's associated infinity category with the stated operad category. All objects are cofibrant since initial maps are monomorphisms. The point model of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] has $C^\natural$ as a cofibrant-fibrant representative of $C$ and associated infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Write $\mathsf K$ and $\mathsf M_P$ for these two models. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] their coherent nerves of bifibrant objects agree with their coherent localizations; this also identifies their enriched sharp mapping complexes with localized mapping spaces.

For $\mathcal O$ with its inert marking form $X=C^
atural	imes\mathcal O$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and take a functorial fibrant replacement $X\xrightarrow{\sim}RX$ in the model category of step 1. This constructs $C\odot\mathcal O$. The marking on $X$ is exactly the conjunction specified in the statement. Each fixed-input product functor is left Quillen by the pushout-product axiom in [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus], since the other input is cofibrant. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to its ordinary right adjoint in each variable. These derived functors are computed on the displayed product, and localizing its replacement map gives an equivalence $qX\simeq qRX$. Any other weak-equivalence map from $X$ to a fibrant object gives the same localized object. The external product preserves weak equivalences in either cofibrant input, so its localization is a bifunctor; the functor-category universal property of localization makes its coherences and the replacement comparisons natural, rather than unrelated choices on objects. atural$. These are the two adjunctions explicitly supplied by the marked enrichment. The localization universal property used here, on entire functor infinity categories, is [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]; applying it in each variable to this weak-equivalence-preserving product gives its coherent bifunctor and natural replacement comparison.

source.place: Remark 3.2.12 and proof of Lemma 3.6.8, pp.609,619

proof.text: For fibrant $\mathcal Q$, the right adjoint to $(-)\times\mathcal O$ is the marked internal Hom $H(\mathcal O,\mathcal Q)$ of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. Its underlying $n$-simplices are maps $(\Delta^n)^b\times\mathcal O\to\mathcal Q$ over the base. The marking condition only requires the restriction at each vertex of $\Delta^n$ to preserve inert edges. Therefore its underlying simplicial set is the full functor subcategory on the inert-preserving functors, namely $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal Q)$, including all coherent transformations. Apply that node's enriched fibration axiom to $\varnothing\to\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal Q\to *_{/B}$. The resulting map $H(\mathcal O,\mathcal Q)\to *$ is a fibration in $\mathsf K$. Its fibrant-object description in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] makes $H$ categorical-fibrant with exactly its equivalences marked. The full-subcategory convention used in the simplex identification is [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The derived right adjoint of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] consequently has this infinity category as its value. Its mapping-space adjunction gives exactly the displayed equivalence, naturally in $C$ and $\mathcal Q$. Precomposition in $\mathcal O$ commutes with the product–Hom adjunction: both adjuncts evaluate $(c,o)$ at the value of the same functor. Thus this is also coherent in $\mathcal O$, using the localized bifunctor of step 2.

Fix either $\mathcal O$ or $C$ and denote the corresponding derived product functor by $L$, its derived right adjoint from step 2 by $R$. The source admits small colimits: for operads this is [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]; for $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] to the combinatorial simplicial model $\mathsf{Cat}^+$ of step 1. For a small diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{dom}(L)$ with colimit $d$ and any target $Q$, the coherent adjunction and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give
$$\operatorname{Map}(Ld,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(d,RQ)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(D_j,RQ)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(LD_j,Q).$$
These are the maps induced by the image cocone, hence the same node's colimit criterion proves that cocone colimiting. This proves separate preservation, also for the empty diagram; no claim that the literal product is already an operad is used. The passage from the localization convention of the derived adjunction to the coherent-nerve convention of the diagram-model theorem is the natural equivalence in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization].

proof.text: Fix $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and the ordinary-operad pattern from step 1. Its base, cone family and finite cone shapes are $\mathcal U$-small. [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] gives common generators and replacements and preservation of weak equivalences of smaller objects. For a $\mathcal U$-small coherent diagram of operads, choose the strict enriched presentation $F:I\to\mathsf M_P$ and $u:\mathfrak C[K]\to I$ supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams], in the smaller universe. Choose a smaller projectively cofibrant replacement $QF\to F$. [lem-coef-projective-diagram-universe-cofibrancy] says that this same replacement is projectively cofibrant and an objectwise weak equivalence in the larger diagram model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-marked-enriched-colimit-universe] to the strict enriched diagram $QF$. Its enriched colimit $L=\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{enr}}_I QF$ and its canonical cocone are unchanged on inclusion, including their universal property against larger targets. Use the common fibrant replacement of [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] to obtain the same fibrant marked object $RL$ in both universes. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams], this is the bifibrant apex representing the colimit in each coherent nerve, with its canonical cocone.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.6 and finite-cone model construction; universe comparison expanded from Higher Algebra B.0.20 proof and the strict diagram colimit construction; the three hidden universe comparisons are now separate statement nodes

proof.text: By [lem-coef-coherent-diagram-universe-naturality], the index $u$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence in both universes, the included strict diagram represents the image of the original coherent diagram, and the included enriched cocone represents its actual image cocone. Thus the two colimit comparisons in the preceding step concern precisely the universe-inclusion image of the given diagram and cocone. The identification of coherent nerves with the localized operad categories is [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. It follows that inclusion of smaller operads preserves the colimit cocone. This applies to every smaller simplicial shape, including the empty shape.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.6 and finite-cone model construction; universe comparison expanded from Higher Algebra B.0.20 proof and the strict diagram colimit construction; the three hidden universe comparisons are now separate statement nodes

proof.text:
Work in $\mathcal U'$ with $C$ and $\mathcal Q$ of that size and the smaller $\mathcal O$ viewed there. [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] gives the marked pattern model there and the product--Hom and product--cotensor adjunctions. Every object is cofibrant, so [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] computes both left derived functors by the marked product and a fibrant replacement. The internal-Hom simplex description still says that each parameter vertex preserves inert edges, hence its underlying infinity category is $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal Q)$ with all transformations. These adjunctions give the displayed mapping-space equivalence in $\mathcal U'$. For either fixed-input derived product $L'$ with right adjoint $R'$, and any smaller-indexed diagram $D$ with colimit $d$ in its containing-universe source, the image cocone gives
$$\operatorname{Map}(L'd,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(d,R'Q)\simeq\lim_j\operatorname{Map}(D_j,R'Q)\simeq\lim_j\operatorname{Map}(L'D_j,Q).$$
The colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] makes that image cocone colimiting. Source colimits exist by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] applied to the containing-universe models. Their localizations and coherent nerves agree by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Steps 5–7 identify the colimit of a smaller operad diagram with its containing-universe colimit, so this calculation also applies to the original smaller operad cocone when $C$ is larger. If both inputs are smaller, the marked product is smaller, and [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] identifies its two fibrant replacements. All mapping spaces here are formed in the containing universe, as asserted.
